# Closet, in full

> A household's wardrobe on its own server: photographed garments, the outfits made from them, a calendar of what to wear, and a wardrobe one person can share with another.

## In short

Closet is MIT-licensed, self-hosted software. It is a progressive web app rendered on the server and meant to be installed on a phone and used by the people of one household. Everything it stores lives in its own PostgreSQL database and data directory on the machine that runs it.

## What it does

### Garments
A garment carries a photo, its category and type, brand, size, colours, care, the date it was acquired and notes. The server cuts each uploaded photo out of its background (BiRefNet) and keeps it as WebP; the browser never processes a photo. Custom categories sit beside the built-in ones, and every one is a filter.

### Outfits
Garments are put together into saved outfits, by hand or from ideas drawn from what the wardrobe holds.

### The calendar
Outfits are planned onto days, a week or a month at a time, and what was worn is recorded.

### Sharing a wardrobe
An invite link gives another account a view of the wardrobe, or the right to edit it.

### Offline and installed
Installed on the home screen, it shows what it has cached without a connection and says how fresh it is. With VAPID keys set it sends Web Push notifications.

### Wears, washes and trips
Wears and washes are logged, availability follows from them, and a trip gets its packing list.

### Wishlist and inspiration
A wishlist holds what to buy next; saved looks can be recreated from the garments already owned.

### Agents
`/mcp` lets Claude and other agents work with the wardrobe through personal access tokens.

### Language
English.

## Pages

- / - Today, the home screen
- /wardrobe - the garments
- /outfits - saved outfits and the outfit builder
- /calendar - the planned week and month
- /about - what Closet is and its licence
- /auth/login - sign in (every page needs it)

## Running it yourself

```bash
docker run --detach --publish 3000:3000 \
  --volume closet_data:/app/data --env DATA_PATH=/app/data \
  --env ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  --env DATABASE_HOST=<postgres host> --env DATABASE_NAME=closet \
  --env DATABASE_USER=closet --env DATABASE_PASS=<password> \
  ghcr.io/kashhq/closet:latest
```

It needs a PostgreSQL database and a session signing secret of 32 characters
or more. The README has a Compose file and every environment variable.

## Built with

- **Licence:** MIT
- **Server:** TypeScript on Fastify, pages rendered as JSX (hono/jsx)
- **Pages:** htmx, Tailwind CSS and daisyUI, all rendered on the server with no client framework
- **Database:** PostgreSQL through Drizzle ORM
- **Photos:** background removal on the server (BiRefNet under ONNX Runtime, in a child process) and sharp for WebP; no photo is processed in the browser
- **Offline:** a Workbox service worker; Web Push
- **Storage:** photo files on local disk
- **Sign-in:** a JWT in a session cookie; every page needs it
- **Shipped as:** a Docker image on GHCR

## Where to find it

- Source: https://github.com/kashhq/closet
- Image: ghcr.io/kashhq/closet
